selected_passages.title: sources/SBF_s_trial_starts_soon_but_how_did_he_and_FTX_get_here
selected_passages.text: Sam Bankman-Fried's criminal trial for seven counts of fraud and conspiracy against FTX has begun, following the exchange's collapse in November 2022 due to severe liquidity issues and mismanagement of customer funds. The once-valued $32 billion crypto empire filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy, leading to the arrest of Bankman-Fried and the guilty pleas of former executives Gary Wang and Caroline Ellison, while the trial proceeds with high-profile legal representation.

Sam Bankman-Fried's criminal trial for seven counts of fraud and conspiracy against FTX has begun, following the exchange's collapse in November 2022 due to severe liquidity issues and mismanagement of customer funds. The once-valued $32 billion crypto empire filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy, leading to the arrest of Bankman-Fried and the guilty pleas of former executives Gary Wang and Caroline Ellison, while the trial proceeds with high-profile legal representation.

- Michael Lewis's book 'Going Infinite' details SBF's rise, his relationship with Lewis, and an alleged $5 billion offer to Donald Trump to cancel his presidential run.
- SBF engaged in significant political maneuvering, meeting with Mitch McConnell and seeking to fund candidates on both sides of the aisle.
- The document highlights public criticism of SBF and the media's coverage, contrasting it with the financial reality of the FTX collapse.
- SBF's company, FTX, collapsed after cryptocurrency valuations fell, leading to accusations of fraud and conspiracy.

selected_passages.title: sources/SBF_s_trial_starts_soon_but_how_did_he_and_FTX_get_here
selected_passages.text:
- Sam Bankman-Fried is currently on trial for seven counts of fraud and conspiracy related to FTX.
- FTX collapsed in November 2022 after exposing a balance sheet showing impossible FTT token holdings.
- Bankman-Fried pleaded not guilty to all charges and faces up to 115 years in prison if convicted.
- Former executives Gary Wang and Caroline Ellison pleaded guilty and will serve as key witnesses.
- The trial is represented by Mark Cohen of Cohen & Gresser, who previously defended Ghislaine Maxwell.
